shared_header_format.confidence: CONFIRMED for field_count/record_count/type-map/row-matrix and pool offsets; word5 remains reserved/unknown
shared_header_format.layout: 6 little-endian uint32 words, then packed 2-bit-per-field type bitmap at +0x18, 4-byte alignment, then row-major int16 token matrix
executable_proof: func_001AD21C returns header+0x4 (word1) as the table record count.
func_001AD180 bounds row_index against word1, computes row_matrix_start = word2 - align4(word0*word1*2), and selects row_matrix_start + row_index*(word0*2).
func_001ACCAC bounds field_index against word0 and reads its 2-bit type code from payload+0x18+(field_index>>2), MSB-first within each byte.

func_001ACD40 resolves the selected row token by type: type 0 = inline signed int16; type 1 = byte/string pool at word4 + token; type 2 = int32 pool at word3 + token*4; type 3 = float pool at word2 + token*4.
Across all 10 decoded XDB tables, word2 - align4(word0*word1*2) exactly equals align4(0x18 + ceil(word0/4)), independently matching the executable layout.
consequences: The old 8-word/32-byte header model is superseded. Bytes at +0x18/+0x1C are type-map/row data, not header words 6/7.
word0=121 in xdbboxr.adf is the number of fields/columns, not the boxer-record count.
word1=37 in xdbboxr.adf is the base table record count.
The old '2-bit flags per boxer record' interpretation is superseded; the 2-bit map classifies fields by storage type.
